record.field: No one can redirect and pay alone

Vendor bank-detail fraud is the top payment-fraud vector. Odoo blocks payments to untrusted bank accounts, but a user who can edit the account, trust it and create the payment bypasses that safeguard alone.
Take "Validate bank account" away from anyone who creates payments; give it to a controller who does not pay. Remove partner-management rights from payment clerks if possible.
Whoever can create users and assign rights can give themselves any permission. They should not also process payments.
Use a dedicated administrator account that is not used for accounting work; remove Billing rights from it.
Odoo's standard Billing role can both enter vendor bills and pay them. Without a second person, a fictitious bill can be entered and paid by one user.
Split bill entry and payment between two people, or add an approval step on payments (e.g. batch payments approved by a manager). Review the money-at-risk events weekly as a compensating control.
No payments to freshly changed bank accounts
Flags outbound payments made within 30 days of the recipient bank account being created or its number changed, the signature of vendor-impersonation fraud.
Call the vendor on a number you already had to confirm the new account, record the call in the event's review note, and mark it legitimate.
Bank accounts verified by a second person
Flags bank accounts that were created or changed and then trusted ("Send Money" enabled) by the same person.
Have a second person re-verify the account with the vendor and re-trust it.
Bills not paid by the person who entered them
Flags payments reconciled with vendor bills entered by the same user.
Review each event against the purchase order or contract and the vendor's delivery; assign payment to a second person going forward.
Flags posted vendor bills with the same vendor, amount and reference (or date) as an earlier bill.
Confirm with the vendor, then reverse the duplicate with a credit note if it was not legitimate.
